summary:
RESEARCH ONLY, 2026-10-17. Nothing was bought, installed, signed up for or committed, and the repo was not edited. I read the PlantCatalog species PDF and the e-on EULA PDF in memory, and saved one plain-text copy of the EULA for the planner at C:/Users/yorki/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-yorki-Desktop-Goldenmaplelandscaping-ca-golden-maple-landscaping/a99e8b7c-9122-4e38-97d0-59c8dc02db01/scratchpad/eon_eula.txt. My operating rules allow only one short verbatim quote per answer, so licence clauses are paraphrased with their section numbers and URLs. The one verbatim quote is in the e-on route. The shared web-search budget ran out near the end. Three things are still unverified: the Florasynth export licence, the species in PlantFactory's stock content, and the Leafsnap dataset licence.

HEADLINE
1. The biggest new free find is e-on PlantFactory and PlantCatalog. Bentley Systems stopped developing e-on software in May 2024 and made VUE, PlantFactory and PlantCatalog free and perpetual for commercial use (https://www.bentley.com/products/e-on-software/).
   - PlantFactory is a VFX-grade botanical plant modeller. Its EULA (https://www.bentley.com/globalassets/content/eula-for-e-on-products.pdf, §2.2) lets you share or sell assets you build in it, so self-built species models are clean for a public repo and a public web app.
   - It is the strongest $0 route to photoreal versions of all 26 species. The cost is skilled manual authoring plus species-accurate leaf textures.
2. The free PlantCatalog library is final at release 2023.3, with about 190 entries. Among the 26 species it covers only Picea pungens, in three cultivars.
   - It does offer useful genus stand-ins: Thuja plicata for Smaragd foliage, Dryopteris, Blechnum and Asplenium ferns, and Festuca and Phalaris grasses.
   - Its exported assets may not be sold. Public-repo distribution is a grey area under EULA §6, so serve them from a non-public origin, or use the official CC BY 4.0 Sketchfab uploads.
3. There is still no free or CC0/CC BY library at species level for the other 25 species.
   - I swept every Poly Haven model, all ambientCG atlases, ShareTextures, ffishAsia (Latin and Japanese names), PlantCatalog's 2,306 Sketchfab uploads, the top-liked Sketchfab CC BY and CC0 plants, and botanic-garden and museum scans. None has more than genus-level coverage.
   - The scan-quality CC0 material (ffishAsia, ambientCG multi-angle atlases, Poly Haven) is best used as texture and bake sources, not as runtime meshes.
4. Free engine and marketplace content cannot go into a public three.js app.
   - Electric Dreams and Valley of the Ancient are marked UE-Only on Fab.
   - Legacy Megascans claimed under the Unreal Engine plan are UE-Only, and free Megascans claimed without a plan are for internal evaluation only (Epic Content License, Megascans Content Addendum §1c and §1e).
   - The current Fab Standard License (EULA updated 1 Oct 2024) has three problems for DeckCraft. §4c requires you to stop end users extracting Content, which a browser-served GLB cannot do. §6(b)(iii) bars Content in world- or level-editing or modelling tools that allow export, and DeckCraft is a design tool. §5a bars standalone distribution, which a public repo would be.
   - Unity's Book of the Dead uses the Asset Store EULA: embedding in an application is fine, a public repo is not. Its species do not match and it is HDRP-only.
   - The Omniverse downloadable packs no longer list any vegetation pack.
5. Blender Studio films, Blender demo files and Poly.pizza are licence-friendly (CC BY or CC0) but stylized or generic. They fail the photoreal bar.
6. Owner-captured species atlases are the only route that gives exact cultivars with clean rights. Timing matters: today is 17 Oct 2026 in Ontario. Evergreens (spruce, pine, cedar, boxwood, yew) can be shot now. Summer foliage and flowers of the deciduous shrubs, trees and perennials cannot be captured until about late May to July 2027, unless a greenhouse or nursery has forced stock.

RECOMMENDED FREE STACK FOR THE PLANNER
- Geometry: build species in PlantFactory, exported as FBX, converted in Blender to GLB, with LOD0, LOD1 and a billboard or impostor LOD2. Use the in-repo generator or ez-tree (MIT) only where PlantFactory is overkill.
- Textures: owner-shot leaf, needle, flower and bark atlases, colour-checked. Fill gaps with CC0 iNaturalist photos, ambientCG multi-angle leaf sets, Poly Haven bark and twigs, and ffishAsia CC0 bakes.
- Picea pungens: the PlantCatalog CC BY Sketchfab model (Koster 12/43) is public-repo-safe with attribution. The free PlantCatalog export at RT resolution can serve it instead, from a non-public origin.
- Nothing goes into the 340 KB viewer chunk. All of this is build-time asset work.

PAID LEADS SEEN IN PASSING (outside this free sweep; any purchase needs owner approval)
- Florasynth: $8 per month for the browser tool, or $45 one-time for the developer licence (its own FAQ also says $50). It exports GLB with LODs. Its licence for exported textures is unpublished.
- Megascans on Fab: plants listed from about $1.40 to $7.05, as displayed from this machine and probably in CAD. The licence is still unusable for DeckCraft, as explained above.

routes.name: Bentley e-on PlantFactory (free since May 2024): self-built species models
routes.what:
PlantFactory is the node-based botanical plant modeller that e-on used to build PlantCatalog. Bentley stopped selling and developing e-on software in May 2024 and now gives away perpetual free licences, including for commercial use (https://www.bentley.com/products/e-on-software/ and https://www.bentley.com/software/e-on-software-free-downloads/).

Versions:
- PlantFactory 2023 is the last stable release.
- PlantFactory 2024 is shipped as an unfinished beta.

Features relevant to photoreal plants, from Bentley's FAQ release notes:
- Cutout Leaf, which builds a leaf from a photo and alpha, with a 3D mesh-edit mode.
- Leaf-cluster baking, including baking textures from a cylindrical photogrammetry mesh.
- Baking of backlight (translucency) into a texture.
- Selectable mesh resolution, LOD conversion through the host-app plugins, and Pivot Painter wind data.

Export formats from the archived product page: FBX, OBJ, ABC, DAE, 3DS, C4D, LWO, GoZ and USDA/USDC/USDZ. There is no glTF export.

It runs on Windows 8, 10 and 11 and on macOS 10.14 to 12. No online activation is needed.
routes.species_coverage: Any of the 26 can be built at species and cultivar level. The tool contains no target species ready-made: PlantCatalog has only Picea pungens (see the next route), and I could not verify which species ship in PlantFactory's stock content because the search budget ran out. Species accuracy depends entirely on the leaf, needle, flower and bark textures you supply and the branching you author.
routes.realism:
PlantCatalog is the ceiling for what this engine can produce: botanically accurate, VFX-grade vegetation. Examples, all CC BY on Sketchfab:
- Blue spruce: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/8c114e3b958e48298a97cc5da6efb1f0
- Male fern: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/5186272e16e3414e9240e093f37c3bf3
- Northern red oak: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/b7ed18f291c3445a8b805da379e3de4f

Honest caveat: getting 25 new species to that standard is skilled manual work for a PlantFactory artist. Realism will be capped by texture quality: owner-shot or CC0 photos need cut-outs, a normal map and translucency.
routes.licence:
e-on Software EULA (Bentley): https://www.bentley.com/globalassets/content/eula-for-e-on-products.pdf
- §1.5 defines 'Software' as VUE, PlantFactory and PlantCatalog.
- §1.9 defines 'User Made Assets' as any procedural or static model files, textures and meshes created using the Software.
- §2.1 grants a free-of-charge, non-exclusive right to install and use.
- §2.2 bars selling assets wholly or partly derived from PlantCatalog assets, materials or texture maps. It permits "sharing or selling User-Made Assets created in VUE or PlantFactory" in generic 3D formats.
- §5 bars renting the Software or providing commercial hosting of it.
- §6 bars distributing the Software itself.

Bentley FAQ (https://www.bentley.com/products/e-on-software/):
- Commercial use is allowed, including exported assets.
- Stock content shipped with VUE and PlantFactory, meshes and textures included, may be retextured, remodelled and resold.
- To sell your own plants, build them from scratch without PlantCatalog textures or metanodes.

Result: scratch-built species models (and stock-content derivatives) can be committed to the public repo and served to browsers. Keep PlantCatalog textures and metanodes out of them.
routes.cost: $0 for the software (perpetual free licence). The real cost is authoring time: PlantFactory has a learning curve and is a GUI tool that agents cannot easily drive.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Download the PlantFactory and VUE installers from https://www.bentley.com/software/e-on-software-free-downloads/ and accept the EULA. Accepting the EULA and installing are owner actions. The page lists no download sizes.
2. Decide who authors the models: in-house, or a hired PlantFactory artist. Hiring is a spend and needs approval.
3. Supply species photos (see the owner-captured atlas route).
4. Optionally ask Bentley to confirm the public-repo position in writing. That is outreach, so it is an owner action.
routes.web_fit:
Pipeline: export FBX or OBJ, convert in Blender (5.2 is installed locally) to GLB, then quantise with meshopt and build KTX2 textures. Resolution is user-set.

Per-plant targets:
- Trees: LOD0 about 12-25k tris, LOD1 about 4-8k, LOD2 a billboard or impostor.
- Shrubs: LOD0 about 4-10k tris.
- Perennials and grasses: LOD0 about 1-4k tris.

Textures: atlas to 1k KTX2 per species. PlantFactory saves textures to disk per material, so atlasing is a build step.

The showcase LOD0 for 273 plants at about 8k average is about 2.2M tris, which the path tracer can handle for stills. Effort is high: roughly half a day to two days per species for a skilled artist (my estimate, not a vendor figure).
routes.risks:
- Discontinued software: no support beyond possible critical security patches, and the 2024 release is a beta. Install the 2023 release beside it.
- No glTF export. FBX import into Blender can mangle alpha-cut leaf materials and needs checking.
- GUI-only authoring makes automated or agent-driven generation impractical.
- Using any PlantCatalog metanode or texture taints the asset under §2.2.
- I could not determine which species the stock content covers.

routes.name: Bentley e-on PlantCatalog (free library, final release 2023.3)
routes.what:
A procedural .tpf plant library, opened in PlantFactory, VUE or the PlantCatalog Exporter. Each plant has presets for age, season, health, forest or open-field shape, and blossoms or fruit.

Resolutions, from the archived product page (https://web.archive.org/web/20231209122945/https://info.e-onsoftware.com/plantcatalog/):
- HD up to 5M polygons.
- LD up to 1M.
- RT (real-time) up to 50k.
- FG with full 3D pine needles.

All releases from 2019.1 to 2023.3 are free downloads. The full species list, dated 05/10/2023, is archived at https://web.archive.org/web/20231209122945/https://2770315.fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net/hubfs/2770315/Plant%20Catalog/plantcatalog_species_2023.3.pdf.
routes.species_coverage:
At species level, only Picea pungens: the species, 'Koster' and 'Glauca Globosa'.

Genus or role stand-ins:
- Thuja plicata (western red cedar): scale-leaf sprays for the Smaragd cedar.
- Picea abies, P. mariana and P. engelmannii, plus the dwarf spruces 'Maxwellii', 'Nidiformis' and 'Ericoides'.
- Ferns for the ostrich fern: Dryopteris filix-mas, Blechnum spicant and Asplenium scolopendrium. They are a different family, but the vase form is similar.
- Grasses: Festuca glauca, Festuca arundinacea and rubra, Phalaris arundinacea, and a generic lawn engine. None is one of our three grasses.
- Hardy shrubs outside the list: Rhododendron catawbiense, 'Nova Zembla' and 'Boule de neige'.
- Ontario-relevant extras: Quercus rubra and Q. palustris, Tsuga mertensiana, Salix and Populus.
- Ground covers and perennials: Vinca minor, Lupinus polyphyllus, Chamerion angustifolium, Calluna, Erica and Vaccinium myrtillus.

Not present:
- Any Acer.
- Pinus strobus. Its pines are contorta, ponderosa, jeffreyi, elliottii and pinaster.
- Amelanchier, Cercis, Buxus, Taxus, Physocarpus, Cornus, Hydrangea, Spiraea and Syringa.
- Any of the 9 target perennials, or the 3 target grasses.
routes.realism:
Among the most realistic procedural vegetation ever sold. The archived page says the species were designed by a landscape architect with textures sourced from arboretums. Seasons and health are parametric.

Examples: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/8c114e3b958e48298a97cc5da6efb1f0 (Koster) and https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/ca883f209e3c469e9f2b29363ef4f0f3 (mature blue spruce).
routes.licence:
Same EULA as PlantFactory: https://www.bentley.com/globalassets/content/eula-for-e-on-products.pdf.
- §1.5 includes PlantCatalog in 'Software'.
- §2.2 bars selling any asset wholly or partly derived from PlantCatalog assets, materials or textures.
- §6 bars distributing the Software, in whole or in part, without Bentley's written permission.

Bentley FAQ (https://www.bentley.com/products/e-on-software/): PlantCatalog is freeware, but the plants remain Bentley's copyright. Commercial use is allowed, for example embedding the models in games, sharing them with clients, or embedding them in project files. Reselling derived models on marketplaces is not.

Result: browser runtime in DeckCraft fits the 'embed in games' wording. Committing exported meshes and textures to a public GitHub repo, where anyone can take them, is a grey area under §6. Serve them from a non-public origin, or use the CC BY Sketchfab uploads instead.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Download the PlantCatalog archive installers and PlantFactory, and accept the EULA (owner).
2. Optionally email Bentley about public-repo distribution of exported models (outreach, so owner).
3. Approve a non-public asset origin, such as a private bucket or CDN path kept out of git.
routes.web_fit:
Export at RT resolution (up to 50k) or a custom resolution, then decimate to about 10-20k tris LOD0 for Picea pungens. Build LOD1 and a billboard. PlantCatalog's own RT versions include camera-facing billboard geometry.

Sketchfab reference: the HD-at-40% Koster 12/43 is 44,675 faces with 20 textures and 9 materials, in a 57 MB GLB. Textures must be atlased to 1k KTX2. Effort is moderate for the spruce. The stand-in species add work.
routes.risks:
- Licence grey area for a public repo, as above.
- No further releases or support.
- Some presets are winter, dead or stump variants, so choose by preset rather than size.
- Exporting needs the Windows or macOS desktop app.
- Do not mix PlantCatalog textures into scratch-built PlantFactory species, or those species lose their resale and sharing rights under §2.2.

routes.name: PlantCatalog official Sketchfab uploads (CC BY 4.0), full census
routes.what: The official e-on/Bentley 'PlantCatalog' account on Sketchfab: https://sketchfab.com/PlantCatalog. I enumerated it through the Sketchfab search API on 2026-10-17. It holds 2,306 models, and every one is labelled 'CC Attribution'. They are fixed exports at about 40% of HD, many with LODs.
routes.species_coverage:
67 species names. Relevant to us:
- Colorado Blue spruce: 44 models.
- Colorado Blue spruce Koster: 43.
- HD Globosa Colorado Blue spruce: 9.
- Black spruce: 45. Norway spruce: 39. Engelmann spruce: 46. Maxwell's Norway spruce: 9. Bird's Nest spruce: 7. Blue Nest spruce: 8. Mountain hemlock: 36.
- Male fern: 37. Common polypody fern: 45.
- Northern red oak: 144, plus seedlings, branch and leaf litter.
- Rosemary willow: 92. Lombardy poplar: 73. Black poplar: 100. Red horse chestnut: 35.

The rest are palms, succulents and tropical plants. Only Picea pungens is one of the 26.
routes.realism:
Very high. These are PlantCatalog HD exports. Examples:
- https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/8c114e3b958e48298a97cc5da6efb1f0 (Koster 12/43: juvenile, thriving, 3.1 m, winter preset).
- https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/ca883f209e3c469e9f2b29363ef4f0f3 (41/43: mature, 7.4 m).
- https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/32e73f7c100e44768370b12bff737d34 (black spruce).
routes.licence: CC BY 4.0, as labelled on each Sketchfab model page (for example https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/8c114e3b958e48298a97cc5da6efb1f0). CC BY allows sharing and adaptation, including commercially, with attribution and an indication of changes (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The licensor is the rights holder's official account, so the CC BY grant here is more reliable than the e-on EULA for public-repo use.
routes.owner_actions: Downloading from Sketchfab needs a logged-in account, so the owner logs in and downloads. List each file's name, source and size before downloading. Add attribution such as 'PlantCatalog by e-on software, CC BY 4.0, modified' to ATTRIBUTION.md and the site credits.
routes.web_fit: GLBs are 23-105 MB with 13-30 textures. The Koster 12/43 is 44,675 faces and 57,131,704 B. They need decimation to about 10-20k tris, an LOD1 and a billboard, and 1k KTX2 atlases. Medium effort for one species.
routes.risks:
- Only one of the 26 species.
- Fixed presets: pick summer or healthy ones and avoid the dead or stump presets, such as Koster 43/43.
- Heavy textures.
- Attribution has to be maintained.

routes.name: Owner-captured species atlases (photos plus free photogrammetry), fed into PlantFactory or the in-repo generator
routes.what:
Shoot every species at a nursery or a consenting client yard, the way Megascans and ambientCG build their atlases:
- Detached leaves, needle sprays, flower heads and grass plumes on a backlit light pad, for alpha and translucency.
- Several raking-light shots for a photometric-stereo normal map. ambientCG calls this method 'PBRMultiAngle'.
- Cross-polarised or diffuse shots for albedo, with a colour checker in frame.
- Bark close-ups.

Optional photogrammetry of low clump forms (hosta, daylily, boxwood globe) as bake sources:
- Meshroom/AliceVision (open source).
- COLMAP (open source).
- RealityScan 2.0: free for individuals and businesses under US$1M revenue in the past 12 months, otherwise US$1,250 per seat per year (https://www.realityscan.com/license).
routes.species_coverage: All 26 at species and cultivar level, including Smaragd, Annabelle, Karl Foerster, Densiformis or Hicksii yew, and purple or green ninebark. Ontario-grown material, with summer and autumn variants.
routes.realism:
The highest attainable at leaf level. It is the same capture method as the CC0 multi-angle sets on ambientCG (for example LeafSet027, LeafSet022 and LeafSet029 at https://ambientcg.com/list?q=leaf+set).

Whole-shrub or tree photogrammetry is not photoreal at runtime: foliage fuses into blobs with baked lighting, as the ffishAsia meshes show (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/4a8be7619bc0468894a19b8f2464947f). Use scans only as bake sources.
routes.licence:
The owner holds copyright in his own photos and derived textures, so they can be committed to the public repo, optionally dedicated CC0.

Caveats:
- Shooting in client yards needs the client's permission. Keep house numbers, people and identifiable property out of frame (privacy).
- I could not retrieve RealityScan's EULA terms on output ownership. Meshroom and COLMAP outputs are unencumbered.
routes.cost: $0 in software with Meshroom or COLMAP, or RealityScan if revenue is under US$1M. A phone or camera, an LED light pad and a colour checker are needed. I did not price them, and any purchase needs approval. Staff time is about 1-2 hours of capture per species, plus processing.
routes.owner_actions:
1. Schedule shoots. Evergreens can be shot now (Oct 2026). Deciduous foliage, flowers and perennials need late May to July 2027, unless forced greenhouse stock is available.
2. Get nursery or client permission.
3. Approve any small equipment purchase.
4. Decide whether to CC0 the resulting atlases.
routes.web_fit: Produces exactly the atlases the build pipeline needs: alpha, albedo, normal and translucency, packed into 1k KTX2 per species family. No runtime cost. Leaves come at their true botanical size.
routes.risks:
- Seasonal timing.
- Colour honesty: needs a colour checker and white balance under Neutral tone mapping.
- Processing labour, such as photometric-stereo scripts or Materialize-style tools.
- Privacy in client yards.

routes.name: ambientCG leaf atlases (CC0)
routes.what:
30 'LeafSet' atlases (LeafSet001-030) plus PineNeedles001 and Foliage001-008 grass and weed atlases. Many are scanned:
- creationMethod 'PBRPhotogrammetry' (for example LeafSet014, 016, 017, 018, 023 and 024).
- creationMethod 'PBRMultiAngle' (LeafSet012, 022, 025-030).

The API returns no species names and no descriptions. Example zip sizes:
- LeafSet022 1K-JPG: 4,312,892 B.
- LeafSet023 1K-JPG: 5,730,325 B.
- LeafSet027 1K-JPG: 4,685,585 B, with 2K at 12.2 MB.
- PineNeedles001 1K-JPG: 4,105,317 B.

API: https://ambientcg.com/api/v2/full_json?type=Atlas
routes.species_coverage:
Unlabelled. Tags name only maple (LeafSet027, autumn orange, 90x90 cm sheet), oak (LeafSet012 and 016), ivy (017 and 029), dandelion (020), needles (019) and grass (026).

Thumbnail impressions, unverified:
- LeafSet018 and LeafSet022: elliptic leaves with arcuate veins, Cornus-like.
- LeafSet023: cordate, acuminate, entire leaves that could stand in for Syringa or Cercis.
- LeafSet019: flat conifer sprigs.
- LeafSet025: a palmately lobed garden leaf.

Use them as genus-level stand-ins only, and verify each by eye before use.
routes.realism: High at card level: scanned albedo, normal, roughness and opacity, and the multi-angle sets have true normals. Generic species. The maple set is in autumn colour, so it does not suit summer without honest recolouring.
routes.licence: CC0 1.0 Universal (https://docs.ambientcg.com/license/). The page says the assets can be copied, modified and distributed, even commercially, without permission. It says raw files may be included in a project such as a video game, and credit is not required.
routes.owner_actions: Approve each download, listing the file name, source and size. The API gives exact sizes.
routes.web_fit: Already atlases. Repack to 1k KTX2 and dilate colour under the alpha. Small and ready for the build pipeline.
routes.risks:
- Species identity is unverified, so do not label a stand-in as the true species.
- Autumn colouration on several sets.
- The opacity in some 'PBRApproximated' sets is synthetic.

routes.name: Poly Haven (CC0): every plant and tree model, checked
routes.what:
All 521 models were checked through https://api.polyhaven.com/assets?t=models on 2026-10-17.

Trees:
- tree_small_02 (Burkea africana, 4.65M tris).
- fir_tree_01 (7.85M), fir_sapling (433k), fir_sapling_medium (2.31M).
- pine_tree_01 (17.4M), pine_sapling_small (398k), pine_sapling_medium (9.78M).
- island_tree_01, 02 and 03 (1.76M-4.76M).
- jacaranda_tree (312k).
- quiver_tree_01 and 02, searsia_burchellii (1.43M), searsia_lucida (842k), othonna_cerarioides.
- dead trunks and stumps.

Shrubs, perennials and grasses:
- shrub_01 (Ageratina adenophora, 282k), shrub_02, 03 and 04 (unnamed; 52k, 17k, 48k), shrub_sorrel_01, wild_rooibos_bush.
- didelta_spinosa, leipoldtia_schultzei, crystalline_iceplant, cheiridopsis_succulent.
- anthurium_botany_01, calathea_orbifolia_01, pachira_aquatica_01.
- nettle_plant, weed_plant_02, periwinkle_plant (67k, pink flowers), celandine_01, dandelion_01.
- fern_02 (6,232 tris), moss_01.
- grass_medium_01 and 02, grass_bermuda_01.
- five Namaqualand flowers.

Textures: no leaf atlases. Bark sets include trident_maple_bark, pine_bark, knotted_pine_bark, japanese_cedar_bark and chinese_cedar_bark. Bed and ground sets include wood_chips, yellow_flower_mulch, raked_dirt and forest_leaves_02, 03 and 04.
routes.species_coverage:
None of the 26 at species level. Usable roles:
- Pine and fir twig and needle cards (genus Pinus, unnamed species) for white pine and the conifers.
- fern_02 as a generic fern.
- grass_medium blades.
- Bark.
- Mulch and leaf-litter ground rings.
routes.realism: Excellent, photoscan-grade texturing (Rob Tuytel and Rico Cilliers photography). Example: https://polyhaven.com/a/pine_sapling_small. Meshes are far too heavy for runtime.
routes.licence: CC0 (https://polyhaven.com/license). The page allows any purpose, including commercial use, and redistribution, including inside products that are sold. Attribution is not required.
routes.owner_actions: Approve downloads, listing file name, source and size. The API gives per-file sizes; for example, the pine_sapling_small 1k glTF .bin is 17,771,796 B.
routes.web_fit: Use the textures and twig cards, not the meshes. Re-card onto the build-time skeletons at 1k KTX2.
routes.risks: No target species. Today tree_small_02, an African tree, drives every deciduous plant in the repo; that is the root of the look the owner rejected.

routes.name: ffishAsia-and-floraZia CC0 scans (Sketchfab), re-checked
routes.what: Thousands of CC0 photogrammetry scans of Japanese flora. I re-queried the account for every target genus in both Latin and Japanese names, including イチイ (Taxus), ツゲ (Buxus), ギボウシ (Hosta), クサソテツ (Matteuccia), ザイフリボク (Amelanchier), ハナズオウ (Cercis), シモツケ (Spiraea japonica), ノリウツギ (Hydrangea paniculata), ライラック (Syringa), ニオイヒバ (Thuja occidentalis), トウヒ (Picea) and カエデ (Acer). Account: https://sketchfab.com/ffishAsia-and-floraZia
routes.species_coverage:
Confirms the earlier findings and adds nothing at species level. Genus-level hits:
- Acer palmatum, A. pictum and Acer sp.
- Hydrangea macrophylla and H. luteovenosa.
- Spiraea thunbergii and S. dasyantha. There is no S. japonica.
- Cornus kousa and C. macrophylla.
- Hemerocallis: six scans.
- Miscanthus sinensis.

New stand-in: 'Japanese Torreya, Torreya nucifera' (https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/f9a37d494bee40b39bd6960dd5f4fd63, 238,930 faces). It is in the yew family (Taxaceae), with flat two-ranked needles, and is a texture stand-in for Taxus alongside Cephalotaxus.
routes.realism: Photoreal from the scanned viewpoint, with baked light. Foliage is fused into dense meshes of 200k to 2.8M faces and 15 to 225 MB, so this is a bake source, not a runtime mesh.
routes.licence: CC0 Public Domain, as labelled on each model page (for example https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/f9a37d494bee40b39bd6960dd5f4fd63). The CC0 deed is at https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/.
routes.owner_actions: Sketchfab login to download (owner). List each file before downloading.
routes.web_fit: Bake leaf and flower textures from them in Blender at build time. They do not ship as meshes.
routes.risks: Genus-level only. Their home site asks that the media not be used for AI training (site text, not the CC0 licence), which does not affect rendering.

routes.name: Sketchfab CC BY and CC0 plants ranked by likes, focused on scans
routes.what:
Queried the Sketchfab API on 2026-10-17: downloadable models, sorted by like count, in the Plants & Trees category and by keyword.

The top-liked CC BY items are mostly stylized or whole scenes, for example 'Low Poly Tree Scene Free' (4,022 likes). Realistic or scanned standouts:
- 3dhdscan 'Simple grass chunks': 3,697 likes, 77,966 faces, 15 textures, 4K. https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/eb4f6dc9d4e3455ea3435385faf58b60
- 3dhdscan 'Leaves in the garden' (984 likes, 519,858 faces) and 'Clover Spring' (908 likes).
- 3dhdscan 'Trees in the park Anthropos': 836 likes, 283,410 faces, an RC scan of winter trees.
- rigsters 'Skovfogedegen oak tree': 704 likes, 54,484 faces, scan. https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/fd582b0d4a8c4af1a1b5c4f21a481c93
- matousekfoto 'Plane tree trunk' (674) and 'Cherry tree' (368).
- Nicholas01 'More Realistic Trees Free!': 1,183 likes, 1,376,186 faces; species and creation tool not stated.
- Jagobo 'Maple Trees': 667 likes, about 50k tris per tree, autumn red, generated with florasynth.com, species not stated. https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/9f51e08e56cd4e44b35fd02a3ad8d3a6
- SanForge '3D Bush - 01': 539,134 faces, 'made from scratch'.

The top CC0 items are almost all ffishAsia scans plus Smithsonian and DigitalAtlasOfAncientLife fossils.
routes.species_coverage: None of the 26 beyond what the earlier research found (PlantCatalog spruce, ASMA3D white pine saplings, maksm Spiraea japonica, LOLIPOP lilac and others). The grass chunks give generic lawn-grass ground cover for bed edges.
routes.realism: The grass chunks and Skovfogedegen oak are true scans. Their single-object realism is good, but foliage on tree scans is poor. Nicholas01 and Jagobo trees are card-based and semi-realistic, with unknown species.
routes.licence: CC BY 4.0, as labelled on each model page. Attribution is required. Provenance is unconfirmed for Nicholas01 (no tool stated) and for Jagobo, whose trees come from Florasynth, a tool with unpublished export terms.
routes.owner_actions: Sketchfab login for downloads. Before shipping any Nicholas01 or Florasynth-derived model, have the owner ask the author about the tool and rights (outreach).
routes.web_fit: Grass chunks: decimate to 2-5k tris and use 1k textures. The rest are too heavy or the wrong species.
routes.risks: Provenance gaps, wrong species, and the attribution burden.

routes.name: ShareTextures foliage atlases
routes.what:
10 species-named foliage atlases (https://www.sharetextures.com/atlases/foliage):
- Robinia viscosa 1, 2 and 3.
- Morus alba 1 and 2.
- Platanus occidentalis 1.
- Nerium oleander 1 and 2.
- Gardenia urvillei 1.
- Avena sativa 1.

The Nature model category has 36 models, almost all stones and rocks. Downloads are gated behind a 'watch a short ad' modal.
routes.species_coverage: None of the 26. Platanus occidentalis is native to southern Ontario but is not on the list.
routes.realism: Photo-based leaf atlases with good, species-named detail.
routes.licence:
A 'Custom CC0' with extra restrictions (https://www.sharetextures.com/p/license):
- Free for commercial use without attribution.
- No redistribution of the assets on other websites, in plugins or as part of collections without written permission.
- No automated downloads or hotlinking.
- The CC0 grant covers only files downloaded directly from the site.

Committing raw atlases to a public repo is plausibly 'redistribution on other websites'.
routes.owner_actions: Downloads go through ad-gated pages. Ask for written permission if public-repo use is wanted (outreach).
routes.risks: Not true CC0, and no target species. Low value.

routes.name: Open-source procedural tree and plant tools (skeleton generators)
routes.what:
- Blender Sapling Tree Gen: GPL-3.0-or-later, version 0.3.7, Blender 4.4+, 35.4 KB. Parametric curve trees. https://extensions.blender.org/add-ons/sapling-tree-gen/
- Modular Tree (mtree): the add-on is GPLv3 and the Mtree C++ library is MIT. Trunk and branch meshes only. https://github.com/MaximeHerpin/modular_tree
- ez-tree: MIT, npm @dgreenheck/ez-tree 1.1.0 (from the earlier research).
- friggog tree-gen: GPL-3. Output may not be sold directly as assets (earlier research: avoid).
- 'Geometry Node Tree v0.1.0' on booth.pm: GPL nodes, CC0 meshed output, stylized.
- Blender demo 'Tree, Leaves and Grass' by Simon Thommes, Blender Studio: CC0, 1 MB, geometry-nodes demo. https://www.blender.org/download/demo-files/
routes.species_coverage: No species out of the box. They provide branching skeletons for any tree. Species identity has to come from parameters plus leaf, needle and bark atlases.
routes.realism: Not photoreal on their own: skeletons with generic or no leaves. Realism depends on the atlases and the shading, so they are at best the structure layer under owner-shot or CC0 textures.
routes.licence: GPL applies to the add-on code, not to the meshes you generate, except that tree-gen restricts direct sale of output. MIT for ez-tree and the Mtree library. CC0 for the Blender demo file.
routes.owner_actions: None for MIT or CC0 code used at build time. Installing Blender add-ons locally is an owner-approved install.
routes.web_fit: Run at build time only and export GLB with custom LODs. Zero runtime cost if the generator is not shipped.
routes.risks:
- The output looks procedural unless crown envelopes and leaf cards are species-tuned.
- No grass, perennial or flower authoring: PlantFactory or hand-built cards are needed for those.

routes.name: Florasynth (paid lead, licence unclear)
routes.what:
A growth-simulation tree generator (https://florasynth.com/): light competition, apical dominance, branch drop and similar. It has 13 species presets, a forest simulation, a wind rig, and LODs down to a 6-triangle billboard with cards baked from the tree's own foliage. It exports OBJ and glTF.

Pricing (https://florasynth.com/purchase):
- Browser: $8 per month, including all presets and textures.
- Developer: $45 one-time for the Blender plugin, Python and C++ bindings, a JS/WASM npm package and linked libraries. The FAQ on the same page says $50.
routes.species_coverage: Unknown. The 13 presets are not named on the pages read. Jagobo's maples were made with it, with species unstated.
routes.realism: Semi-realistic to good, depending on textures. Example: https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/9f51e08e56cd4e44b35fd02a3ad8d3a6
routes.licence: No published terms for exported trees or bundled textures; /terms returns 404. The FAQ only says the developer licence allows embedding the generation libraries in commercial software and client work.
routes.cost: $8 per month or $45-50 one-time (needs owner purchase approval)
routes.owner_actions: Approve the purchase. Ask the author in writing about rights to exported meshes and textures for a public repo and web runtime (outreach).
routes.web_fit: Strong: glTF export with LODs and billboards, and a JS/WASM library that could run at build time.
routes.risks: Unpublished output licence, a small one-person vendor, and price inconsistency on the page.

routes.name: Blender Studio open-movie assets and Blender demo files
routes.what:
Blender Studio production files for Sprite Fright, Spring, Wing It!, DOGWALK and Charge. The vegetation libraries:
- Sprite Fright: oak trees and bark, foxgloves, bracken, bluebells, harebells, cow parsley, dandelions, moss, ferns, bush and branch libraries (https://studio.blender.org/projects/sprite-fright/trees/ and https://studio.blender.org/films/sprite-fright/plants_and_fungi).
- DOGWALK: pine, birch, willow, reeds, grass and small-bush libraries (https://studio.blender.org/projects/dogwalk/3dbec25770ea22/).
- Charge: pitched at PBR realism, but I found no vegetation library; only a free 'Charge Material Asset Library'. https://studio.blender.org/films/charge/

Most items are marked 'Subscribe to view'.

Blender demo files (https://www.blender.org/download/demo-files/):
- 'Tree, Leaves and Grass' (CC0, 1 MB).
- 'Flower Scattering' (CC0, 6 MB).
- 'Ball in Grass Interaction' (CC-BY, 200 KB).
- 'Red Autumn Forest' splash (CC-BY-SA 3.0).
routes.species_coverage: None of the 26. Oak, bracken, foxglove, bluebell, birch, pine and willow are all off-list.
routes.realism: Stylized: Sprite Fright, Spring, Wing It and DOGWALK are cartoon productions. The demo files are generic geometry-nodes examples. Fails the photoreal bar.
routes.licence:
Studio content is generally CC BY (https://studio.blender.org/remixing/). The Wing It! licensing page (https://studio.blender.org/projects/wing-it/pages/licensing/) states CC BY 4.0, with commercial reuse allowed with attribution '(CC) Blender Foundation | studio.blender.org'. Logos and trademarks are excluded.

Demo-file licences are per file as listed on the demo-files page. Red Autumn Forest is CC-BY-SA, which is outside the owner's CC0/CC BY rule.
routes.cost: Blender Studio subscription: $17 per month, or $34.50 per quarter ($11.50 per month) (https://studio.blender.org/join/). Demo files are free.
routes.owner_actions: A subscription purchase would need approval. Not recommended.
routes.web_fit: .blend files that need export work. Irrelevant species.
routes.risks: Stylized look, wrong species and a paywall. No value for the photoreal goal.

routes.name: Megascans and Fab (free samples, legacy free-for-Unreal Megascans, Fab freebies)
routes.what:
Megascans moved to Fab in October 2024.
- Free for all engines until the end of 2024. From 2025 most of the library is paid; Epic announced $0.99 per asset, $4.99 per kit and $24.99 per pack.
- Free Megascans samples still listed on Fab: Dark Ruins, Medieval Village, Military Trench, Derelict Corridor, Goddess Temple and 'Ground Cover'.
- Paid Megascans plants exist, for example 'Boxwood', displayed from this machine at $1.40, $5.64 or $7.05 (probably CAD).
- I found no Megascans hosta.
routes.species_coverage: The free samples are not garden species. The paid Megascans catalogue has some relevant genera (Boxwood seen), but the licence blocks DeckCraft use regardless.
routes.realism: Excellent, scan-based. The licence is the blocker, not quality.
routes.licence:
Fab EULA, last updated 1 Oct 2024 (https://www.fab.com/eula):
- §2.a: the Personal tier requires under US$100k revenue in the digital content industry.
- §4.c: interactive Projects may include Content only as object code, and you must stop end users from extracting it or using it outside the Project.
- §5.a: no standalone distribution except to collaborators.
- §6(b)(ii): no 'stand-alone basis' transfer.
- §6(b)(iii): Content may not be made available in world- or level-editing tools, templates or modelling tools that allow works to be exported.
- The Fab summary (https://www.fab.com/cla) says use is not limited to Unreal Engine.

Legacy Megascans fall under the Epic Content License (https://www.unrealengine.com/en-US/eula/content), Megascans Content Addendum:
- §1c: content acquired on the Unreal Engine plan is UE-Only.
- §1e: content acquired with no plan is for internal evaluation only.
- §1a: Personal-plan content may not be distributed in source format.
routes.cost: Free samples cost $0. Paid assets cost about $0.99 or more each (displayed in CAD on this machine).
routes.owner_actions: None recommended. Any purchase would need approval and legal review, and is not advised.
routes.web_fit: Would need conversion from UE or FBX. Moot.
routes.risks:
- GLBs served to a public web app are trivially extractable, which breaches §4c.
- DeckCraft is a design tool, which falls under §6(b)(iii).
- A public repo is standalone distribution under §5.a.
- Legacy UE-plan Megascans are UE-only.

routes.name: Unreal Electric Dreams and Valley of the Ancient sample projects
routes.what:
Epic's free sample projects on Fab.
- Electric Dreams Env: a jungle built from Quixel assets and PCG. https://www.fab.com/listings/d79688f5-29be-4fb2-a650-2d4a813f5306
- Valley of the Ancient: a desert, 205 GB of storage. https://www.fab.com/listings/0c19880e-21bd-42ba-8287-1caccc3951b1
routes.licence: The Electric Dreams listing says 'UE-Only Content - Licensed for Use Only with Unreal Engine-based Products'. The Valley of the Ancient listing says its content is licensed for use only with Unreal Engine-based products. The Epic Content License §5a defines UE-Only Content (https://www.unrealengine.com/en-US/eula/content).

routes.name: Unity Book of the Dead: Environment and Terrain Sample Asset Pack
routes.what:
Book of the Dead: Environment (https://assetstore.unity.com/packages/slug/121175): free, 2.7 GB, version 1.1 (24 Mar 2023), HDRP only, Unity 2022.2.9. It contains Quixel-scanned forest content and is listed as license type 'Extension Asset'.

The Terrain Sample Asset Pack (https://marketplace.unity.com/packages/3d/environments/landscapes/terrain-sample-asset-pack-145808) contains heightmaps and terrain layers, with no vegetation. Its height data is under ODbL.
routes.species_coverage: Book of the Dead species are not listed on the pages I read; it is a forest set, with no evidence of any of the 26. The Terrain pack has no plants.
routes.realism: Photoreal scans, but built as an HDRP showcase.
routes.licence:
The official forum FAQ (https://discussions.unity.com/t/book-of-the-dead-environment/705542) says the Quixel content is under the standard Asset Store EULA.

Asset Store EULA (https://unity.com/legal/as-terms):
- §2.2.1(a) allows incorporating an Asset, with substantial original content, into an electronic application as an embedded component.
- §2.2.1(b) allows distribution only as incorporated and embedded.
- §2.2.1.1(d) forbids any other distribution.

No engine lock, but a public repo of the raw assets is not allowed.
routes.owner_actions: A Unity account and the Unity Editor would be needed to extract the assets. Not recommended.
routes.web_fit: Unity prefabs and SpeedTree-style materials would need conversion. Low value.
routes.risks: Wrong species, an HDRP extraction burden, and the 'Extension Asset' licence type is unexplained.

routes.name: NVIDIA Omniverse sample content
routes.what: The current Omniverse 'Downloadable Asset Packs' page (https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/usd/latest/usd_content_samples/downloadable_packs.html) lists over 250 GB of packs. They cover scene templates, commercial, industrial, residential and warehouse assets, SimReady sets, sample scenes, rigged characters, data centre, materials, skies, AEC and workflow samples. There is no vegetation pack. Omniverse vegetation comes through the e-on PlantCatalog and PlantFactory connectors, which are the PlantFactory and PlantCatalog routes above.
routes.licence: The pack descriptions say 'free to use in your work'. The NVIDIA Omniverse licence pages returned HTTP 403 to my fetches, so the Content clauses could not be read. The earlier research also found no asset-level redistribution licence.
routes.risks: No vegetation, and the licence is unreadable. Skip.

routes.name: Poly.pizza
routes.what: A free low-poly model library: Poly by Google archive, Quaternius and others. Example: 'Spruce tree' by Poly by Google, tagged Low Poly Nature, OBJ/glTF (https://poly.pizza/m/ahT2_ZxtLIq). A maple search returns Quaternius 'Maple Trees' and Google Poly maple, ash, elm, beech and spruce trees.
routes.species_coverage: Named genera (maple, spruce, pine, birch, beech, oak), but stylized.
routes.realism: Low-poly and stylized. Fails the photoreal bar.
routes.licence: Per model. The example page states 'Creative Commons Attribution' (Poly by Google items are CC BY); Quaternius items are CC0.
routes.web_fit: Tiny glTFs, but useless for realism.

routes.name: Botanic garden and museum open scans (Kew, Smithsonian, arboreta)
routes.what:
Searched Sketchfab (CC0 and CC BY) for Kew Gardens, botanic or botanical garden, arboretum, herbarium and Royal Botanic, and checked user accounts for 'kew'. Finds:
- kungphil 'Old sweet chestnut tree in Kew Gardens' (CC BY, 0 faces, so a point cloud).
- Smithsonian CC0 orchid 'Embreea herrenhusana'.
- DigitalAtlasOfAncientLife CC0 fossils.
- 'Pierandrea Matthiolus's Herbarium', a book.
No botanic-garden collection of living garden plants under an open licence.
routes.licence: Per item: CC0 or CC BY, as labelled on Sketchfab.
routes.risks: Dead end. Herbarium sheets elsewhere (pressed, discoloured) are useful only for leaf silhouettes.
